title: Internal Hom under the open-subscheme equivalence
statement: For an open U of a scheme Y, the equivalence between modules on the over-U site and modules on U carries internal Hom to internal Hom, naturally in both arguments.

proof.text: Construct the comparison by reindexing compatible local linear maps along Over.post U.overEquivalence.inverse. Its injectivity follows from faithful whiskering. Full whiskering supplies the inverse additive natural transformation; essential surjectivity and naturality along an object-preimage isomorphism transport scalar compatibility to every object, proving surjectivity. Pointwise bijectivity gives a presheaf isomorphism, lifted through fullyFaithfulForget to a sheaf-of-modules isomorphism.
Precomposition and postcomposition commute with this fixed reindexing map componentwise by definitional equality, giving naturality in both arguments.

lean.statement:
theorem internalHom_overEquiv {Y : Scheme.{u}} (U : Y.Opens) :
    let F := (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).functor
    ∃ e : ∀ (A B : SheafOfModules.{u} (Y.ringCatSheaf.over U)),
      F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf.over U) A B) ≅
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf) (F.obj A) (F.obj B),
      ∀ (A A' B B' : SheafOfModules.{u} (Y.ringCatSheaf.over U))
        (f : A' ⟶ A) (g : B ⟶ B'),
        F.map (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf.over U) f g) ≫
            (e A' B').hom =
          (e A B).hom ≫
            SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf)
              (F.map f) (F.map g)
